parole.significato: harsh, hard, strict, stern [with allative ‘to’ or (partitive +) kohtaan] (of a person or character, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *angazaz (compare English anger, Swedish ånger). Cognate with Karelian ankara.

parole.significato: in someone's possession, custody or care
parole.testo: From *haltu- + -ssa (inessive singular), with the root borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *haldaną (compare English hold, German halten, Swedish hålla).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚺᚨᛏᛏᚢᛉ (*hattuʀ) (compare Swedish hatt), from Proto-Germanic *hattuz (compare English hat). Cognate with Ingrian hattu, Karelian hattu.

parole.significato: a slippery layer or cover of ice
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *hēlijaz) and derived with + -ma. Cognate with Karelian kaljama.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo) (perhaps more specifically from a form with -ll-, compare Old Norse skalli (“skull, a bald head”), Swedish skalle (“skull”)), from Proto-Germanic *skallô.

parole.significato: stick, billet (small, solid piece of wood, often shaped for a useful function)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚲᚨᛒᚢᛚᚨ (*kabula), from Proto-Germanic *kablaz; compare Swedish kavel, kavle and Norwegian kavl.

Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *skaidaz; compare Swedish skede (“span of time”). No cognates are found in other Baltic-Finnic languages. Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᚲᛟᚱᛟ (*skoro), from Proto-Germanic *skurō.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gulju), from Proto-Germanic *guljō, whence Alemannic German Gülle and Swedish göl.

parole.significato: to stop, cease, come to an end, end, finish
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *slakōną (compare *slakaz, whence slack), and derived with + -ata.
From laup- + -ias, the root being borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *laubō, *laubą (“permission, favour”).

Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛗᛟᚱᚦᚨ (*morþa), from Proto-Germanic *murþą (for *þ > *h, compare huopa), SSA however instead opines that the word may be a back-derivation from murhe, with influence in meaning from the Germanic word. If a loan, doublet of marras.

parole.significato: a place to sit on by a (traditional) oven or stove
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*bankā), from Proto-Germanic *bankô; seemingly adapted with + -kko.
Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *barilaz. Cognate with Karelian parilas.

parole.significato: embankment, dyke, bank (steep slope of earth, sand, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old East Norse *benkr), from Proto-Germanic *bankiz. Doublet of penkki, pankko, and penkka.

parole.significato: tail (of a bird or a marine animal)
parole.testo: Fronted from pursto, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *burstō, *burstiz (“bristle”).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚱᚢᚾᛟ (runo), from Proto-Germanic *rūnō (“letter, literature, secret”), possibly from Proto-Celtic *rūnā. Compare English rune and Swedish runa.

parole.significato: seam (folded back and stitched piece of fabric)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*saumaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *saumaz.

parole.significato: a kind of tent or canopy held over the couple during a wedding ceremony
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛏᛖᛚᛞᚨ (*telda), from Proto-Germanic *teldą. Doublet of teltta.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*þinga), from Proto-Germanic *þingą.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*dōgi(a)ʀ) (from Proto-Germanic *dōg-) and further derived with + -io.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᚨᛗᛗᚨᛉ (*wammaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *wammaz (“spot, stain, blemish”).
vako(i)- + -ta, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wakāną (“to wake, to be awake, to watch”).

parole.significato: to wait for, await (to expect someone to come or something to happen)
parole.testo: varro- + -ta, the root being borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wardāną.
